title: Role implication map + quick-assign rail for member role edits
creator: Anika Patel
description: Design a contextual 'Role Implication Map' and a persistent 'Quick-Assign Rail' that surface the downstream effects of role edits when assigning roles to members. Goals: reduce accidental over-privilege, make assignments auditable and reversible, and surface audit-logging and temporary grant options inline.
background: RBAC v2 introduces more composable role rules (resource scoping, conditional grants, and temporal roles). Customers frequently report uncertainty about implied permissions when assigning roles. Current role editor shows role details but doesn't visualize cross-role collisions or effective permissions at the member level. This leads to help-desk tickets and manual audits. We need a lightweight, keyboard-accessible UX that fits inside the Console member page and scales to tenants with hundreds of roles.
design_goals: Preview effective permissions for a member before change is committed
Highlight permission overlaps and risky escalations using a defined risk taxonomy
Allow safe temporary grants with automatic expiry and audit metadata
Provide a compact, keyboard-first quick-assign rail that persists during multi-member workflows
Link each assignment to the audit log entry and the change diff for quick review
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a role shows an implication map: explicit permissions, inherited permissions, and resource scope visualized
The UI warns when a role grants permissions outside the member's current scope with a clear risk label
Admin can toggle 'simulate effective permissions' to view a pre-commit diff showing net permission additions and removals
Temporary grants are creatable from the rail with a duration picker; grant creates an audit entry with expiry metadata
Quick-assign rail persists while navigating between members and supports keyboard shortcuts (G to open, Enter to confirm, Esc to cancel)
Every confirmed change includes a link to the generated audit log entry and a permalink to the diff in the activity timeline
user_personas: Platform engineer managing role assignments across 10+ product teams
Security admin approving temporary elevated access for on-call engineers
Product manager reviewing role changes during a rollout
proposed_flow_steps: Open member detail -> Quick-assign rail auto-opens on right edge (G opens via keyboard)
Search and select roles; each selection adds a stacked chip and updates the implication map
Use 'Simulate' toggle to render a permission diff (added/removed) grouped by resource and risk level
Choose 'Temporary' to add expiry and optional justification; preview shows audit metadata that will be recorded
Confirm -> show success toast with 'View audit entry' link -> audit entry appears in timeline with change diff and metadata
visual_components: Right-side Quick-Assign Rail (320-420px) with stacked role chips; top area shows member summary; mid area shows role search and selected chips; bottom area shows compact implication map (three columns: explicit, inherited, simulated net) with colored risk badges; sticky confirm bar with duration and justification controls.
accessibility_notes: Rail must be keyboard-navigable and screen-reader friendly. Simulate toggle announces changes via live region. Color must not be sole cue for risk; use icons and text labels (High/Medium/Low).
design_constraints: Must reuse existing Console tokens and chip components
Implication map must compute and render within 200ms for members with up to 100 roles (avoid blocking main thread)
Rail should not push content on small screens; fallback to modal when width < 960px
privacy_and_audit_considerations: Temporary grant flow writes an audit record containing executor, target member, role(s), justification, expiry, and simulation snapshot. Audit entries must be immutable and surfaced in the timeline with TTL-based archival policy as per compliance requirements.
open_questions: Should 'Simulate' call the same effective-permissions engine used by the backend SLO? (ENG dependency: ENG-8270)
How granular should risk taxonomy be (3 levels vs 5 levels)? Security prefers 5 for precision but UI may be noisy
Do we auto-suggest least-privilege role alternatives when high-risk is detected? If yes, what ranking signals do we use?
decisions: Simulate will use a cached call to the backend with a 10s timeout; if it times out, show partial results and allow confirm with warning
Risk taxonomy initial rollout will use 3 buckets (Low/Medium/High) with icons and tooltip rationale
Quick-assign rail will fallback to modal on narrow screens to avoid layout breakage
tradeoffs: Showing a full permission tree improves clarity but risks overwhelming users; we opt for summarized grouped view with 'drill into resource' links
Running live simulation per role selection provides immediate feedback but increases backend load; solution: debounce and cache results per member session
Auto-suggesting safer roles reduces escalations but could hide necessary roles; we will A/B test suggestion aggressiveness
dev_notes: Backend needs a stable /simulate-effective-permissions endpoint with input: member_id, [role_ids], and option: include_inherited=true. ENG-8124 will surface permission deltas. Client must handle 202 accepted with async polling. Include telemetry events for simulate_open, simulate_run, assign_confirm, temp_grant_created.
security_notes: All quick-assign actions must be logged with actor IP and SSO session ID. Temporary grants must validate expiry on the server and enforce removal by the scheduler (cannot rely solely on client-side TTL).
qa_criteria: Simulate shows correct net additions for combinations of roles in a fixture with inherited rules
Temporary grant expires at the intended timestamp and appears as revoked in audit timeline
Keyboard flow: G opens rail, Arrow keys navigate list, Enter selects role, Esc closes and preserves unsaved selections per session policy
release_notes_draft: Console: added Role Implication Map and Quick-Assign Rail to help admins preview effective permissions and create temporary grants inline. Includes audit links and simulation mode to reduce accidental over-privilege.
risks: Backend simulation performance could degrade at scale leading to poor UX
Admins may over-rely on simulation and skip manual reviews; mitigation: require justification for high-risk confirms
Complex role graphs might still be misinterpreted; mitigation: provide inline 'explain why' for each implied permission
